Novel

/NOV-ul/ — rhymes with shovel · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is novel is new and original, unlike anything experienced before.

Using drones to plant trees is a novel approach to reforestation.

Worked Example

Using drones to plant trees is a novel approach to reforestation, combining aerial technology with environmental restoration in a way foresters had never attempted.

Novel is more precise than 'new' because it captures not just newness but originality and creative difference. 'New' only means recently made; novel means new AND original AND unexpectedly fresh.

How Novel Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

new

new: recently made or just now appearing

original

original: the first of its kind, not copied

innovative

innovative: introducing clever new methods or ideas

Antonyms

conventional

conventional: following the usual, accepted way of doing things

hackneyed

hackneyed: overused so often it feels stale

How Strong Is It? — ordinary → new → original → novel

ordinary vs. novel

ordinary vs. novel: Ordinary sits at the opposite end of the scale from novel: an ordinary idea is the usual kind everyone expects, while a novel one has never been tried before.

new vs. novel

new vs. novel: New is weaker than novel; something new is simply recent, but a novel idea is not just recent — it is unlike anything that came before.

original vs. novel

original vs. novel: Original is strong, but novel goes a step further: an original idea is not copied, while a novel one feels strikingly fresh and previously unknown.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — nov

Root — nov: new (from Latin novus) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Novel comes from Latin novus, 'new' — its diminutive novellus meant 'new and young,' and the -el ending is the fossilized remnant of that Latin form. Something novel is so new and original that nothing quite like it has been experienced before.

Use the root in a new word: renovate

Use the root in a new word: renovate: When workers renovate an old house, they literally make it new again — the same Latin root nov, meaning 'new,' that appears in novel.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Use novel when you mean something is not just new but creatively different and unexpectedly original. If you simply mean something was recently made or invented, 'new' is simpler and often better.
